cases.refreshed: Offered in English or Tiếng Việt. Do you need help using a computer? Want to set up an email account? Stop by the Santa Teresa Branch Library for a session with our experienced volunteer! They can assist you with basic tech issues, such as: Setting up an email account, composing & sending emails, using email attachments; Web searches and basic data entry; Learning the basics of Microsoft Word and Excel and web-based productivity software such as Google Docs; Using the library's pay-for-print and photocopy machines; Downloading apps on your phone or tablet; And much more! You are welcome to bring your own device, such as a laptop, phone or tablet, or you can use one of our computers. Free. No registration required.

events.title: Robotics Workshop: Presented by Power Beans Foundation

cases.refreshed: In this full day workshop with the Power Beans Foundation, participants will get hands-on experience building and programming robots and will learn: Robot design and engineering principles; Hands on VEX V5RC Robot Building; Programming with VEX Code; Teamwork and Collaboration skills. Participants will work in teams to build their robots, program them, and showcase their robot in a friendly competition towards the end of the program. Requirements: Lunch is scheduled in the middle from noon to 12:30 p.m. Please bring your own lunch. A signed waiver will be required before participating in this program. Copies will be emailed and available upon arrival. Participants must be ages 10 and up. Registration: Registration is required. Registered participants will receive a detailed agenda of the program. Registration opens November 4, 2026 at 9 a.m.

cases.refreshed: Storytime is a fun and interactive experience designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. This program promotes the joys of reading and learning for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Stay after storytime for our Stay and Play session, where kids can enjoy hands-on activities, toys, and social playtime together. Free, with limited capacity. Seating is first come, first served. The library hands out a limited number of tickets at the information desk 30 minutes before storytime. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.

cases.refreshed: Be part of a fun volunteering opportunity for teens between the ages of 13 and 18. Earn community service credit while supporting the library by assisting with library programs, promotion, and representing the library's teen point-of-view. Learn about teen volunteer opportunities and more by attending our monthly meetings and have your say! Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. If you are new to volunteering with San Jose Public Library, please check out Teens Reach: Community Service for more information. If you wish to apply, click "Sign Me Up" under Willow Glen Branch Library.

cases.refreshed: Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ Maker Space! Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, Glow Forge, Sewing & Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Each machine and other materials have limitations and time requirements. Pre-registration is recommended to reserve your spot. If registered participants have not arrived by 4:30 PM, their spots will be given to those waiting. All services are provided for free to middle and high school students (grades 6-12). Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. Pre-registration will start 1 week before the start of the program. Please un-register yourself if you find you're unable to attend at a later date. Registration closes 1 hour before the start of the program. There will not be a waitlist for pre-registration. Drop-ins will be accepted if not all registration slots are filled and if not all registered individuals arrive by 4:30 PM. The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children's Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available upon request. Please note that each device requires time to set up, use, and complete whatever task you're wanting to use the space for. Be sure that you have enough time in your schedule to attend the program. Not all tasks may be completed before the end of the program and you may need to return to get your completed items or pause your task and restart at another studio session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility. 3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 4.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and the time needed to complete prints are not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 4.5 hours. Poster Printing: All prints must be assembled on a 2"x3" canvas and printed as a PNG file. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. Glow Forge: Create a custom engraved object. Object should follow similar guidelines to the Custom Keychain Program. Complexity of request is at the discretion of the librarian. Sewing & Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. Scrap material and thread are available, but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board are also available. Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you'll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If you bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameters in inches. Small Button Press: 1.25"; Large Button Press: 2.25"; Picture Size: 1.156"; Cut Line: 1.629"; Picture Size: 2.063"; Cut Line: 2.625".

cases.refreshed: Buddy up with a furry friend and read aloud from your favorite book! Practice your reading skills and build up your self-confidence reading to a patient and furry listener. This program is for children who have completed kindergarten through 5th grade. Parents are asked to remain in the library during the 20-minute program. Registration opens the 3rd Monday of the month. Children must register for this program in person at the Children's Reference Desk, and may register for one reading session each month. Thank you to Furry Friends P.A.T.S. (Pet Assisted Therapy Services) - www.furryfriends.org - for co-sponsoring this program. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
